items.prompt: What does the usual finite-variance iid Monte Carlo standard error measure?

options.text: Repeated-run spread of the simulated mean around its model target
options.why: It is the standard deviation of the estimator under the stated model.

options.text: A guaranteed upper bound on this run's absolute error
options.why: An error can exceed one or several standard errors.

options.text: Whether the model matches a live market
options.why: Sampling precision does not validate the model.

options.text: The spread of the unaveraged payoff with no n adjustment
options.why: A mean has its own variance, σ²/n under these assumptions.

items.explanation: The model, target function, sampling mechanism and finite variance are part of the standard-error claim.
